title: Project memory audit findings
description: The one finding shape every auditor tier must satisfy. The Codex tier receives this file through --output-schema, so the model cannot emit anything else; the Gemini tier has no schema flag and is validated against this same file after the fact. That is deliberate: tier two must not be able to return a looser shape than tier one. Because Codex passes this to a structured-output decoder, the file stays inside the strict subset that decoder accepts -- every object sets additionalProperties to false and lists every one of its properties in required, and no string constraints beyond enum are used. Adding a keyword outside that subset breaks the Codex tier, and scripts/auditor-bridge.mjs fails loudly rather than silently skipping it.

summary.description: One paragraph on what was checked and what was not checkable from available evidence. Not a verdict: an audit that found nothing wrong has still only examined what it could observe.

findings.description: Every claim the evaluator examined and has something to say about. An empty array is a valid answer and means no finding was supportable by evidence -- it does not mean the memory tree is correct.

finding.description: The specific memory claim under judgement, quoted or paraphrased tightly enough that a reader can locate it. Not a category, not a summary of several claims.

classification.description: How the claim stands against current reality. VALID: holds. STALE: was true, no longer is. CONTRADICTED: current evidence directly refutes it. UNVERIFIABLE: cannot be checked from available evidence -- this is an honest answer, not a failure. DUPLICATED: asserted in more than one artifact. MISPLACED: true, but living in the wrong artifact. TOO_VERBOSE: correct but consuming disproportionate context. MISSING: should be recorded and is not.

artifact.description: Repository-relative path of the memory artifact the finding is about, for example memory/current-state.md. For a MISSING finding, the artifact that should carry the claim.

evidence.description: What was actually observed, with file paths and, where they exist, line numbers, commit ids, or command output. A judgement without an observation behind it is not evidence and should not be reported.

confidence.description: How strongly the evidence supports the classification. Reserve high for a direct observation; use low rather than omitting a finding you are unsure of.
